questions.stem: What is the primary use of the Inverse Fourier Transform in signal processing?

choices.A: Converting a continuous-time signal to a discrete-time signal.
choices.B: Determining the frequency content of a signal.
choices.C: Reconstructing a time-domain signal from its frequency domain representation.
choices.D: Filtering out unwanted noise from a signal.

questions.solution: The Inverse Fourier Transform is used to reconstruct a time-domain signal from its frequency domain representation. It helps in understanding how the signal varies over time based on its frequency components.
questions.explanation: A: The Continuous-Time Fourier Transform does that, not the Inverse Fourier Transform. B: The Fourier Transform determines the frequency content. D: Filtering is an application but not the primary use of the Inverse Fourier Transform.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake is to confuse the roles of Fourier Transform and Inverse Fourier Transform.

questions.stem: Which type of filter can be designed using frequency domain information obtained from a signal?
questions.solution: Butterworth Filters are designed based on the desired frequency response, which can be obtained from the Fourier Transform or Inverse Fourier Transform of a signal.
questions.explanation: B: Mean and Median Filters are non-parametric filters that operate in the time domain. C: Same as B. D: Moving Average Filter is also a time-domain filter.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake is to choose time-domain filters instead of frequency-domain designed ones.

questions.stem: What technique can be used to compress signals in the context of signal processing?
questions.solution: Quantization is a process that reduces the number of bits required to represent a signal, which helps in compression.
questions.explanation: B: Amplitude Modulation changes the amplitude of a carrier wave. C: Frequency Domain Sampling does not necessarily lead to compression. D: Time-Shifting doesn't change the size of the signal.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake is to confuse compression techniques with modulation or sampling methods.

questions.stem: Which method in signal processing is commonly used for noise reduction?

questions.explanation: B: Least Squares Regression is for fitting a line to data points. C: Principal Component Analysis is for dimensionality reduction. D: Independent Component Analysis separates mixed signals.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake is to confuse noise reduction techniques with other signal processing methods.

questions.stem: What technique can be used to smooth noisy signals in the time domain?
questions.solution: Savitzky-Golay Filters are used for smoothing time-domain signals by applying a moving average with polynomial fitting.
questions.explanation: B: Discrete Cosine Transform is a frequency domain transform. C: Fast Fourier Transform is also a frequency domain transform. D: Z-Transform is a mathematical tool, not a signal smoothing method.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake is to choose frequency domain transforms or unrelated methods.

questions.stem: In a communication system, what type of filter would be used to allow only specific frequencies to pass through?
questions.solution: A Bandpass Filter is designed to allow signals within a certain frequency range to pass while attenuating frequencies outside that range.
questions.explanation: A: Low-Pass Filter allows low frequencies only. B: High-Pass Filter allows high frequencies only. D: All-Pass Filter passes all frequencies equally, without attenuation.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake is to choose filters that allow passage of only one type of frequency.

questions.stem: What process in signal processing involves converting a modulated signal back into its original form?
questions.solution: Demodulation is the process of extracting the original information from a carrier wave that has been modulated.
questions.explanation: A: Sampling involves taking measurements at regular intervals. B: Quantization reduces the number of bits to represent a signal. C: Decimation is reducing the sampling rate.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake is to confuse demodulation with other processes related to signal representation.
